Natalie — thanks for sending and for the clear summary. Quick replies:

- Subprocessors: we can commit to 30-day notice plus a right to object for "sensitive" subprocessor categories (as defined by you). We can't accept a hard consent requirement for all new subs since we rely on our GPU infra partners.
- Transfers: our standard approach is SCCs plus our transfer addendum; happy to discuss specific Helix language but would prefer keeping an SCC foundation for speed.
- Breach notification: we can do 24-hour initial notification for incidents that materially impact Helix customers; followed by a substantive update within 72 hours.

I'm looping in Monica and Rachel (privacy counsel) for suggested redline language. See my short notes attached (Rdrw_Privacy_Notes_SG.pdf). If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to go through the non-starters and propose a DocuSign route for execution.

Folks — draft counsel notes below (I kept bullets short so we can paste into a consolidated redline):

1) Subprocessors
- Proposed Redwood language: 30 days' notice + objection right limited to material risk categories (security hosting providers, analytics providers, model training vendors). For other classes, automatic notification and 60-day opt-out to allow contract termination (not consent).
- Rationale: preserves operational flexibility while giving Helix an objection mechanism for critical services.

2) Cross-border transfers
- Recommend offering SCCs (EU standard contractual clauses) + Redwood Transfer Addendum (short, references SCCs and lists our subprocessors). If Helix insists on bespoke addendum, ensure it's non-conflicting with SCCs and we keep the same liability caps.
- Action: attach proposed addendum (Redwood_Proposed_Addendum_vA.docx) to the response and mark as "for negotiation".

3) Breach notification & incident response
- Counterproposal: 24-hour initial notification for incidents that materially affect Helix production data or result in actionable risk; 72-hour follow-up with scope/mitigation steps. Provide SOC 2 evidence via secure link.

4) Escalation & execution path
- Suggest we return a controlled redline (accepting low-risk edits, marking high-risk for counsel review), propose an e-sign envelope to close out the DPA once both sides agree on transfer mechanics.
- Timing: target to circulate Redwood redline to Helix by end of day 11/12 and set a 48-hour review window; call to resolve open items 11/13 morning if needed.

I'll prepare the redline language and the proposed addendum and share AS A COMMENTED DOC for their counsel. LMK if you want me to redact any technical subprocessor names prior to sending.

-Monica

Thanks again for the redline. Attached are two files: (1) Redwood consolidated redline (tracked changes) and (2) Redwood_Proposed_Addendum_vA.docx. Highlights of our position:

- Subprocessors: we accept 30-day notice and an objection right limited to material categories (security hosting, model training vendors). We cannot accept a blanket consent requirement for every new subprocessor.
- Transfers: our proposed path is SCCs + Redwood Transfer Addendum (attached). If Helix prefers bespoke language, we can work through the addendum but ask to preserve the liability and indemnity balance.
- Incident reporting: Redwood will provide 24-hour initial notification for material incidents, followed by a substantive 72-hour update and SOC2 evidence via secure share.

Execution plan:
